clue.text: Make note of scatterbrain kicking out at riots

indicators.note: riots throw order into chaos, so the remaining letters run wild into a new arrangement
kicking something out ejects it, so those letters are thrown out of the word they sit in

parts.note: taken as written, as the fodder
taken as written; these two letters are removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A disorganised person loses their temper over rioting and someone is asked to write it down.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AT from SCATTERBRAIN to leave SCTERBRAIN, then rearrange those ten letters into TRANSCRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To transcribe is to write something down in full, a formal way of recording words heard or read.

clue.text: Heading skywards, alien being in turmoil — first to travel so far

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading upwards means reading from the bottom, so the string runs backwards

parts.note: E.T. is the film's extraterrestrial
ado is fuss or commotion

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word it qualifies

parts.note: opening letter of travel

explanation.surface: An alien rising up in a state of turmoil is the first to travel this far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here; it just runs the pieces on. E.T. is the alien from Spielberg's film.
explanation.definitionFit: To date is an idiom meaning up until now, exactly the sense of so far in a sentence.

clue.text: Scrap of adult feminine wear

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
F is the grammatical abbreviation for feminine
to wear is to fray, as cloth does at the edges

explanation.surface: A scrap of clothing from a woman's wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as a fragment of fabric, which fits 'wear' nicely; it is really a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public brawl, and a scrap is informal slang for a fight or scuffle.

clue.text: Building up to a point, Conservative has energy for 4 …

parts.note: a steeple is a church tower rising to a spire
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A Tory politician has the energy to build a pointed edifice, which runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross-reference: 4 is the answer to 4 down, RACE, and the ellipsis links the two clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a horse or athletics race over fences, hurdles and water jumps.

clue.text: … people — impressive, putting Right on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, placing something on top means it comes first, ahead of what follows

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
ace is slang for excellent or impressive

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: people are impressive when they put the Right in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 3 down, but this clue stands alone; 'Right' looks political, and is only the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A race can mean a people or nation sharing common descent, as in the human race.

clue.text: British want my covering papers — this could be dangerous

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
want in the sense of a shortage
my! and wow! are both exclamations of surprise
identity papers, ID for short

explanation.surface: A Brit wishes their documents were covered, warning that it could be risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is not a possessive but an exclamation of surprise, and 'papers' are identity papers.
explanation.definitionFit: The black widow is a spider with a venomous bite, so a cryptic description of a hazardous creature fits.

clue.text: More than one party clown

parts.note: a do is a party
more than one calls for a second copy of the same word

explanation.surface: Someone who attends several parties is a bit of a clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than one party' asks for the plural idea literally, as two copies of DO set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodo is informal for a stupid or old-fashioned person, a fool much like a clown.

clue.text: Music from orchestra or a small group, with zero content

parts.note: surface padding: it only dresses the scene

indicators.note: content is what a thing holds inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a trio is a group of three
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A piece played by an orchestra or a chamber group, with no real substance to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orchestra' is not an abbreviation here; it is part of the surface, and the wordplay starts at 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical work for voices and orchestra on a sacred theme, such as Handel's Messiah.

clue.text: Means to create trouble after work — time to move as far as possible!

indicators.text: to move as far as possible
indicators.note: moving a letter as far as it can go sends it from the very start to the very end

parts.note: toil is hard work
pain as distress or bother
T is the abbreviation for time; it is the opening letter of the first block, and this is the one moved

explanation.surface: A troublemaker plots mischief after work, then urges everyone to flee as far as they can.
explanation.walkthrough: TOIL then PAIN gives TOILPAIN; the T of time at the front is shifted to the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paint is a medium artists use for creating pictures, so it is literally a means of creation.

clue.text: Very strong in battle, essentially lacking combat gear

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its middle, and lacking it means those central letters are dropped
in places one thing inside another

parts.note: a duel is a fight between two
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
the central MB is removed

explanation.surface: A soldier is fearsome in battle despite having no proper combat kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combat gear' looks like one phrase, but 'combat' feeds the wordplay and 'gear' alone is the definition; FF for very strong (loud) is the musical fortissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear means clothing, and this hooded toggled overcoat of thick wool is one such garment, famously worn by naval officers.

clue.text: Dance and shout in karaoke?

indicators.note: karaoke is performed out loud, so the word is to be voiced rather than spelt

parts.note: to bawl is to shout or yell

explanation.surface: At a karaoke night you might dance and belt out a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose homophone signal: singing in karaoke is a vocal act.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a formal social gathering for dancing, such as a masked or charity ball.

clue.text: There's drilling here — one could get ear pad?

parts.note: surface reading: a site where workmen drill holes, or where an oil rig bores
setter's reading: the answer's first word, mixed up as its second word suggests, would produce the letters of 'ear pad'

explanation.surface: A building site full of noisy drilling, where a worker might want ear protection.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse anagram: PARADE, when ground up, gives EAR PAD, so the answer's second word acts as the anagram signal. Drilling here is soldiers' drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade ground is the open area where troops practise marching and drill exercises.

clue.text: Trim after retirement having taken power walks

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word runs backwards
to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: trim and smart both mean neat in appearance
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A pensioner keeps fit after retiring by taking brisk power walks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' and 'walks' both look like nouns from a fitness article; trim is the adjective SMART and walks is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or trek a long way, so tramps works as the verb walks.

clue.text: Fine rewrite of Alamo winning hearts as musical

parts.note: OK means fine or acceptable

indicators.note: winning something means gaining it, so a piece is taken in
a rewrite changes the text, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A good reworking of the Alamo story wins audiences over as a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a judgement on the rewrite, but it is the first piece of wordplay; the Alamo is the Texas mission famously besieged in 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is the 1943 Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show, one of the best-known Broadway musicals.

clue.text: With a single heart and clubs, North wrapping up after contracted trick

indicators.note: a contracted word is shortened, so it loses its final letter
wrapping up means finishing, so the remaining piece comes at the close

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
once as a conjunction means after, as in 'once you have eaten'
N is the abbreviation for north
trick shortened by its last letter

explanation.surface: A bridge bidding scene: one heart, clubs, and North making the contract after a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge language hides the definition: 'With a single heart' means having one shared centre, not holding one card. 'after' supplies ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentric circles share one common centre point, and heart here means centre rather than a playing card.

clue.text: Protest state's housing is shaming

parts.note: demo is short for demonstration

indicators.note: a house holds its occupants, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: a state is a nation; the 's stands for has
taken as written

explanation.surface: Holding a protest against the government is a way of publicly shaming it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state’s' reads as possessive, but it is 'state has', with the nation housing IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonisation is portraying someone as wicked, a public vilification close in meaning to shaming them.

clue.text: Essential in Serengeti: mile gauge showing elevation, and numerical compass

indicators.note: elevation means rising, and in a down entry rising letters read from bottom to top
something essential in a phrase is contained within it, so the letters sit inside the words

parts.note: the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A safari guide needs a gauge measuring altitude in miles, and a compass, on the Serengeti plains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compass' suggests a navigation tool, but here it means range or scope; the Serengeti is a Tanzanian national park.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass can mean range or extent, and an age limit sets the numerical range of ages allowed.

clue.text: Pet goes on a hunt in tunnels

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is singular; a catacomb is a network of tunnels

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
goes on signals that A follows
to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A pet dog or ferret sets off on a hunt through underground burrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hunt' suggests chasing prey, but it is the search sense, COMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery of galleries and passages, so it is a set of tunnels.

clue.text: Book with numerous strip scenes?

parts.note: surface reading: a racy book full of striptease episodes
setter's reading: comic strips, a book told in many illustrated panels

explanation.surface: A steamy paperback packed with undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip' means comic strip, and the first word of the answer can also mean explicit, which is what keeps the risqué reading alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A graphic novel is a book-length story told in comic-strip panels, so it consists of many strip pictures.

clue.text: Patchwork part of fasCIA SO Messily erected

indicators.note: something erected stands upright, and in a down entry that means the letters read upwards
part of means a run of letters taken from inside the words

parts.note: the end of the first word, the second and the start of the third, picked out in capitals

explanation.surface: A patchwork fascia panel, put up in a messy way.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter prints the hidden letters in capitals as a gift; a fascia is a board over a shop front.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a picture made from small pieces, so it is a patchwork of separate bits.

clue.text: Prove most chunky when topless

indicators.note: topless means without its top, and in a down entry the top is the first letter

parts.note: chunkiest, the superlative of fat

explanation.surface: The heaviest person shows it best by going shirtless.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the F from FATTEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness to or demonstrate the truth of something, so it means prove.

clue.text: Trouble backing this individual? Half of US can work together

definitions.note: a base verb, while the answer is the -ing form

indicators.note: half of keeps only one of two equal parts and throws the other away
backing means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
the setter speaking of themself
a can is a prison; Sing Sing is the famous New York jail, and half of it is used

explanation.surface: Despite trouble with this person, half the US can cooperate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is slang for prison, and Sing Sing is a maximum-security prison in New York State; 'Half of US' looks like U or S, but it governs the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to cooperate and keep in contact with others, so liaising means working jointly.

clue.text: Dropping off regularly at eulogy, brat's shown revolting taste

indicators.note: to revolt is to turn over, so the kept letters run backwards
dropping at a steady interval discards every other letter and keeps the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A child nodding off during a funeral speech shows appalling manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting taste' looks like a phrase about bad behaviour, but 'revolting' is the turnaround signal and 'taste' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A try-out is a trial or sample, and a taste likewise means a small sample to test something.

clue.text: Level, e.g. both teams getting 99 runs

parts.note: when both sides score the same, such as 99 each, the game is drawn
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket match ends level, with both teams scoring 99 runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level' wants to describe the tied scores, which is the wordplay's job; here it is the noun meaning a layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one row or layer in a stack, which is the noun sense of a level.

clue.text: We see this twinkling forth

parts.note: a twinkling is an instant, as is a mo, short for moment
forth and on both mean onward, as in 'and so on'

explanation.surface: Looking up at a star twinkling in the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twinkling' looks like a description of a star, but it is the 'in a twinkling' sense, a brief moment; the definition is deliberately vague.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing most visible in the night sky is our satellite, so a vague description of something seen overhead works.

clue.text: Graffiti maybe seen by one copper delayed express

parts.note: graffiti is an example of street art
Roman numeral one
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: Graffiti on a train spotted by a police officer while the express was running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' and 'express' suggest a policeman and a train; copper is the element and express is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate a thought is to put it into clear words, the same as to express it.

clue.text: An objection over one giving low blows

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the letters run back to front

parts.note: the indefinite article
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a boxer who keeps hitting below the belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low blows' suggests foul punches; it is someone blowing low notes on a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the deepest-pitched brass instrument, so its player blows the lowest notes in the band.

clue.text: Day care cost that's discounted over reconstituted chicken

indicators.note: reconstituting something rebuilds it from its parts in a different form
a discounted price has something taken off, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
cost with its O removed
O is the cricket abbreviation for over; this is the letter discounted

explanation.surface: Nursery fees are cut, set against the price of processed chicken nuggets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' sits beside 'reconstituted' as if it were processed meat; it is the definition, meaning a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for a coward, and a scaredy-cat is the childish word for a fearful person.
